title: Terminal: A window for controlling the computer using commands
body: The Terminal is a window for controlling your computer using commands.
when_to_show: When reviewing terminal, cli, shell, command
detail: Instead of opening folders and running programs with the mouse, you change directories using commands like `cd` or `Set-Location` and run scripts with the `python` command. Developers use the Terminal to repeatedly test, verify, check Git status, and install packages. Beginners often find the error messages displayed on the screen intimidating, but Terminal output provides important clues about where the code went wrong. This card is not just for memorizing definitions; it serves as a supplementary guide to help you understand how variables, data types, functions, files, and API flows are connected in actual Python code.

title: Shell: A program that interprets commands
body: A shell is a program that interprets user commands and passes them to the operating system. Examples of shells include PowerShell, Bash, and zsh.
detail: Developers use shells to navigate folders, check files, run Python, execute Git commands, and install packages. Even for the same command, line breaks and path notation may differ depending on the shell. When running code, you must verify whether you are using PowerShell or Bash, and you must also distinguish whether an error message is due to a shell syntax issue or a Python issue. This card is not intended merely for memorizing definitions; it serves as a supplementary guide to help you understand how variables, data types, functions, files, and API flows are connected in actual Python code.

title: Package Manager: A tool for managing installations
body: A package manager is a tool that manages the installation of necessary libraries. In Python, pip is the most common example, while in JavaScript, tools like npm and pnpm are frequently used.
when_to_show: When reviewing pip, npm, apt, package
detail: Since projects typically depend on multiple external libraries, you must document which packages need to be installed for the code to run. If an `import` fails while reading the code, it may be because the package isn’t installed or the virtual environment is different. You should also check files like `requirements.txt`. When solving a problem, first locate the line in the code where this concept appears, and then categorize that line: is it a step that reads input, changes a value, evaluates a condition, or stores or outputs a result?

title: venv: Python virtual environment
body: venv isolates a project's Python path and package installation location. Activation only changes the current shell's PATH for convenience; code can instead invoke the environment's interpreter explicitly.
when_to_show: Issues with the Python environment and package installation
detail: Verify that installation and execution use the same interpreter with sys.executable and python -m pip.

title: Git: Change History Management
body: Git is a tool for managing change history. When you modify a file and create a commit, you can record the changes made at that point in time, allowing you to track later on which files were changed and why.
when_to_show: When reviewing git, commit, branch, push
detail: Tags are used to assign names to specific commits and establish fixed reference points. If a problem arises during development, use `git status` to check the current state of changes and `git log` to review the previous workflow. When fixing code, it’s important to get into the habit of making small changes, verifying them, and then committing. title: GitHub: A platform for hosting Git repositories
body: GitHub is a platform for hosting and sharing Git repositories. While Git manages the history of changes on your computer, GitHub stores that history remotely and enables you to collaborate with others.
when_to_show: When reviewing github, git, pages, repo
detail: A commit is a group of changes, and a tag is a label assigned to a specific point in time. When reading or modifying code, understanding GitHub and Git allows you to track what changed in each version. title: API Key: A secret key used to call the service
body: An API key is a secret key used when calling external services. The server uses this key to determine who made the request, whether they have permission, and which account to charge for the costs.
when_to_show: When reviewing api_key, env, security, secret
detail: Therefore, it is risky to hardcode an API key directly into your code and upload it to a public repository. Typically, it is stored in a .env file or as an environment variable and is not exposed on the client-side interface. When reading code, you should verify where the API Key is fetched from and ensure it isn’t logged. When solving problems, first locate the line in the code where this concept appears, and then determine whether that line reads input, modifies a value, evaluates a condition, or stores or outputs a result.

title: .env: Secret configuration file
body: A .env file commonly stores local configuration as NAME=value, not only secrets, and Python does not read it automatically. A loader such as python-dotenv is required.
when_to_show: Environment Variables, API Keys, GitHub Issues
detail: Exclude files containing secrets from Git; .gitignore does not remove an already tracked file, and any exposed key must be rotated.

title: Logging: Recording Execution History
body: Logging records stages, timing, counts, and failures at useful severity levels. Check destination, retention, and exception traces, but never record API keys, tokens, or personal data—even at DEBUG. Keep user-facing results separate from diagnostic records.
when_to_show: When reviewing logging, debug, batch, server

title: Debugging: Identifying the Cause of a Problem
body: Debugging is the process of finding the cause of why code isn’t behaving as intended.
when_to_show: When reviewing debugging, error, traceback, log
detail: It involves reading error messages, checking which line caused the failure, and verifying whether variable values differ from expectations. Beginners often assume that if an error occurs, the entire code is wrong, but in reality, the issue is often a small typo, a path problem, a data type mix-up, or a problem with the flow of a conditional statement. When debugging, it’s important to get into the habit of narrowing down the problem by examining the input, intermediate values, and output in that order.

title: API Keys and Security
summary: By default, API keys should not be hard-coded but should be read from environment variables or a secure secret store.
detail: If you hardcode an API key directly into your code, it could be exposed through GitHub pushes, logs, screen sharing, and other means. Generally, os.environ, .env, secret managers, or server-side storage are used. During code reviews, check whether the key is read from a secure source, whether it appears in logs, and whether it is exposed to the client.
body: API keys and security are topics that require careful attention from the very beginning of development. An API key is similar to a secret key that allows you to use external services. If you hardcode this value directly into your code and upload it to GitHub, others could use the service through your account or incur charges. That’s why they’re typically stored in a secret configuration file, such as `.env`, and never committed to a public repository. In code, it’s common to retrieve them from environment variables using functions like `os.environ`. When learning Python, if you see examples where passwords or keys are stored directly in string variables, you should understand that this can be risky in a production environment. When reviewing secure code, check where secret values are stored, whether they appear in logs, and whether they are exposed to clients. When studying this card, don’t just memorize the definitions of the terms; also verify how they relate to specific variables, functions, and data types in actual code. The goal is to apply the concepts you’ve learned from small examples to the data processing and service architecture of real-world projects. When reviewing security-related code, you should start by checking for exposed secret values, permission scopes, input validation, and information logged to the system. It’s also important to ensure that API keys aren’t visible on the screen or in Git, and that failure messages don’t reveal excessive information.
